notes:
Summary: Enterprise payments platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive fraud/risk scoring and conversational flows. Primary ask: firm throughput guarantees (200-500 rps for small batch scorer; 50 rps for chat), tight p95 SLOs (<=120ms for scoring; p99 tail constraints), and deterministic unit economics for committed capacity.

Cost modeling details discussed in workshop: commit tiers of GPU hours mapped to three price bands (Conservative: 30% commit, Balanced: 60% commit, Aggressive: 85% commit). Finance expects utilization assumptions to be explicit: steady-state utilization 60% for Balanced, 45% for Conservative, 75% for Aggressive. We produced a sample unit economics table (rough): cost-per-inference-token estimated at $0.0009/token on A100 baseline @30% commit, $0.00055/token at 60% commit, down to $0.00038/token at 85% commit with model quantization and batching.

Operational asks: dedicated GPU pool with hot-standby across two AZs, autoscale burst to shared pool for peak seasonal surges, KV prefix caching to reduce per-token compute on repeated lookups, inference runtime config pinned by model-version and rollout windows.

SLA negotiation points: financial credits for miss of p95 > 150ms for two consecutive hours, defined measurement hooks (route-level tracing), and required 30-day data residency controls for transaction PII. Legal wants explicit failover ordering and fallbacks to lower-tier model variants.

Quotes / paraphrases: "We need predictable unit cost before we commit — running headless experiments isn't enough for finance — show us the math." — Head of ML Ops.

Actions pending: Redwood to send three-tier SOW with A/B cost columns (A100 vs H100) and per-token math, plus appendix for KMS/HSM flows. SE Diego to run targeted perf tests (50-500 rps) with their sample prompts (provided in Drive).
